disclosure: AI-assisted source-frozen delta reassessment, not an external audit-firm certificate. The reviewer had the prior conversation, finding register and some implementation history; this is neither blind nor independent of all prior development. New executions and contradictory outcomes are recorded separately from inherited evidence. No production transactions, service restarts, contract deployments or product-code changes were performed.
summary: F-20 is verified resolved for its original consume-before-durable-successor cause. F-36, F-08 and F-19 have useful repairs but remain partially mitigated: post-deployment Creator publication can still monopolize the worker; serialized sponsorship effects still couple healthy chains to a stalled broadcast; and logging/escalation is not a controlled financial outcome. A newly demonstrated Low issue, F-40, affects privileged reviewer metadata attribution, not bridge custody. No new Critical or High defect was demonstrated within the reviewed delta. The current 40-cause register contains 10 Medium, 16 Low, 3 Informational and 11 resolved causes. One existing Medium remains an explicitly bounded accepted risk, not a new acceptance.
separation: Neither immutable contract source nor browser application source changed in the remediation delta. A UI/email maintenance commit is not evidence of compromised collateral or BLS forgery. Conversely, node signing, proof-to-wallet binding and service transaction construction retain their real security consequences regardless of directory. Bytecode matching does not prove every mutable configuration value, all historical balances, all validator installations or independence of RPC upstreams.

decisions.basis: No new principal-authorization, collateral-backing or message-forgery regression was demonstrated. Contract source and tracked deployment configuration are unchanged. Preserve authenticated route/asset/ISM bindings, chain-native finality, supported native-recipient restrictions, RPC-witness trust disclosure and supervised recovery/load bounds. The optional-service findings do not by themselves invalidate this core opinion.

decisions.scope: Node v3.5.1 F-20 source and published binary
decisions.decision: F-20 VERIFIED RESOLVED; rollout evidence qualified
decisions.basis: Exact successor payload, signer and on-disk journal checks plus file/directory fsync remove the reviewed original cause. Fresh repeated failure/restart tests pass. The official binary checksum matches its release manifest. Public RPC version observations are mixed; a version banner is not an installed-binary hash attestation and does not prove every validator was updated.

decisions.decision: NO-GO for an all-chain availability/outcome claim
decisions.basis: F-08 and F-19 retain demonstrated operational/control gaps; F-17 also remains. This is not a blanket prohibition on self-funded bridge transfers. Do not delete liabilities or wrap effectful payout in an outer timeout to manufacture availability.

Requires named responsibility, actual outcomes and escalation, bounded servicing, installed restricted-role controls, preserved original nonce/raw transaction, and current reserve/backlog checks. This audit does not accept a policy on the operator's behalf. Merely inserting a reviewer event neither fulfills nor waives a promise.

decisions.decision: NO-GO for an unattended availability claim
decisions.basis: F-36 is still reproducible after an admitted request reaches deployed/publication state. Correctly created tokens and their owner/mint controls were not shown compromised. Supervised operation can be bounded only with journal-preserving recovery and explicit operator handling of F-36/F-37/F-38.

Retain the existing F-09/F-13/F-31 transaction/claim presentation restrictions. Email or layout maintenance is not a protocol exploit. Eight existing fixture/discovery failures remain and must not be hidden behind selected green CI workflows.

evidence.E-01: Frozen Git archives and complete diff inventories from run 43696416777; exact commit/tree and archive hashes retained. Interchain: 235 changed paths, 13 non-audit paths. Node: 13 changed paths, only two Go files. Relevant prior source references: 73 unique files, 66 identical Git blobs and seven changed.
evidence.E-02: Complete file discovery on frozen Interchain in run 43696812308: 174 test files; 166 pass and eight fail; TAP aggregate 1,046 tests, 1,035 pass, 11 fail, zero skipped/cancelled. The eight failing files are the same historical fixture/discovery issues. An initial harness aborted at the first failure; the corrected run explicitly captured all results. Its continue-on-error is evidence collection, not a full-suite pass.
evidence.E-03: Fresh frozen-node test run 43696416777: 495 passing test events, one skipped fuzz seed, zero failing test events, six nonempty packages. Five separate repetitions of the existing F-20 journal test pass. This is not the full consensus/EEST suite or a replay of every historical exploit.
evidence.E-04: Supplemental run 43696812308: five repetitions each of the existing F-20 test and an audit-added blocked-file-write/restart test, ten passes total. Original evidence remains after failed successor write; recovered successor survives old-vote retirement. This exercises logical write failure and restart, not physical power loss or every filesystem failure mode.
evidence.E-05: Fresh Foundry run 43696812357, job 132759080254, synthetic audit merge 835864e7e228bdb10b1854757da120efdcd337b6 with unchanged product sources: 111 tests across 17 suites pass, zero fail/skip. Foundry 1.9.0, Solidity 0.8.24, 82-source import closure; constructor/sealed-build and runtime/initcode eligibility checks pass.
evidence.E-06: Read-only production snapshot 2026-11-15T08:56:28.945Z to 08:56:37.063Z. 101 recorded contracts x two configured endpoints = 202 observations: 119 verified, 83 unavailable, zero mismatches. 78 unique receipts have at least one verification, 41 both. rpc1 advertises v3.5.1; rpc2 v3.5.0. Official release binary SHA256 matches the published manifest. Managed/Join/transfer health respond HTTP 200, but sponsorship aggregate availability is false with Base unready. No production write was sent.
evidence.E-07: Local Node v22.16.0 controlled Creator executions use real admission, email confirmation, queue and manifest validation with mocked mail/RPC/signature/publisher boundaries. Positive control advances a healthy sibling. Two admitted metadata-boundary variants reach deployed state then block three consecutive sweeps and leave a healthy sibling queued. Oversized UTF-8 name now rejects. A separate expired-contact-retention case deletes an unresolved signed record. Zero real sends.
evidence.E-08: Local export-only instrumentation of the exact frozen gas-sponsor module exercises the actual scheduler, local signer and send function with pre-authenticated fixture preflights and mocked DB/network. A stalled first destination broadcast blocks a healthy second effect beyond four read deadlines although both preflights finish. The second effect can start after its fixture parent completes externally while queued; the fresh-send path has no final delivery reread. A timed-out-read negative control still produces zero late sends. This is not an end-to-end source-authentication bypass or mainnet attack.
evidence.E-09: Actual isolated PostgreSQL 16 reviewer role: normal CLI succeeds; UPDATE and private recipient-column SELECT fail with 42501. Direct table INSERT nevertheless accepts a different sponsor, arbitrary reviewer identity and historical recorded_at for an existing grant key. The underlying obligation remains present; no grant/payment mutation is authorized.
evidence.E-10: Local controlled Creator proof test invokes the actual two-RPC verifier with internally consistent but mutually different creation-block hashes at the same height. Normalized comparison accepts both because canonical block identity is omitted. This re-verifies existing F-38; no token-ownership or supply-check bypass is asserted. Zero real RPC calls.

F-01.assessment: The relevant executor, state-transaction and proposal-validation sources remain identical to the prior audited blobs. The original accounting authorization cause remains closed on that evidence; this delta introduces no chain execution change. Original fork/accounting acceptance controls are retained.
F-01.evidence: E-01; inherited original security-accounting evidence, not freshly re-exploited.

F-02.assessment: Original-value tracking and refund-accounting dependencies are unchanged. No change in this delta reintroduces the original cause. Historical closure is carried with explicit unchanged-source provenance rather than claimed as a new whole-EVM proof.

F-03.assessment: Peer checkpoint/governance work still reaches expensive remote evidence paths before complete cheap authenticated admission, while gossip can create independent work goroutines. The F-20 storage change does not add global/per-peer work or proposal-expiry admission bounds. Existing Medium remains open.
F-03.evidence: E-01, E-03; targeted gossip/checkpoint/governance source review. No production load attack.

F-04.assessment: Per-route observer isolation is improved from older baselines, but shared capacity and I/O failure constraints remain. These paths are unchanged by F-20. Repeated current tests do not establish oldest-work progress under sustained capacity saturation.
F-04.evidence: E-01, E-03; observer scheduling and historical limit analysis.

F-05.assessment: External source evidence is compared as complete snapshots across distinct configured witness identities; native XGR uses its local state path. Endpoint/operator labels do not prove independent physical upstreams. The live receipt checks confirm observations, not upstream independence. No new risk acceptance is recorded.
F-05.evidence: E-01, E-03, E-06; rpc_evidence_quorum and direct-signing review.

F-06.assessment: The original missing quote-intent and monitor role grants remain repaired in unchanged migrations. Current role and real-schema tests are positive for the exercised paths. A newly added reviewer-attribution issue is separately counted as F-40; it does not reopen the original SELECT/readiness cause.
F-06.evidence: E-01, E-02, E-09; installed host roles still require operator evidence.

F-07.assessment: Exact signed bytes and the reservation are still committed atomically before broadcast, retaining nonce ownership through uncertain outcomes. The fresh PostgreSQL test verifies duplicate reservation exclusion and persistence after reopening. Do not interpret this as permission to replace unknown sends.

F-08.assessment: The repair provides fair source/destination candidate selection, bounded read-only preparation and parallel destination reads. However all successful send functions share a global effect promise: an unresolved broadcast still blocks another healthy destination. The controlled successful-preflight fixture reproduces this, whereas the new production tests primarily exercise non-authorizing results. Earlier serialized expiry/reconciliation and post-send reads also remain bounded-service concerns. Partial mitigation is real, complete all-chain liveness is not established.
F-08.evidence: E-02 and E-08; actual scheduler/send function, mocked network and pre-authenticated fixture inputs.
F-08.remediation: Keep the read/effect fence. Design independently progressing, chain-scoped transaction lifecycles and bounded transport/receipt handling while preserving exact prepared bytes and nonce ownership. Include a successful healthy payout while another broadcast is unresolved, plus process-deadline and restart tests. Never use an outer timeout to discard uncertain effects.

F-09.assessment: The native router preserves backed pending credits when a recipient rejects bounded-gas delivery, and only the beneficiary can withdraw or redirect. Mailbox completion can still be presented as final principal receipt, and some recipient contracts cannot exercise recovery. Fresh contract tests confirm the escrow/claim safeguards, not universal recipient usability.
F-09.evidence: E-01, E-05; native router and wallet/indexer presentation review.

F-10.assessment: The authorized service-wallet and ownership transition ordering still permits the documented role separation to converge. No public unauthorized takeover is shown; the contract is unchanged and existing source tests cannot make the operating role invariant an enforced invariant.

F-11.assessment: Membership payloads still omit the exact registry deployment address. The historical bounded acceptance remains tied to one active receipt-pinned registry per stated origin/destination domain; this audit neither broadens that acceptance nor authorizes overlapping migration. Transfer messages separately bind their destination ISM/registry.
F-11.evidence: E-01, E-05; unchanged membership codec and historical acceptance.

F-12.assessment: The reviewed registry requires a nonempty eligible committee but does not itself enforce the economically meaningful operating minimum. Quorum arithmetic and proof-of-possession remain verified controls, not proof of sufficient independent operators.
F-12.evidence: E-01, E-05; unchanged registry bootstrap and membership policy.

F-13.assessment: The unchanged wallet-side process calldata path still lacks full correspondence with the specifically selected transfer intent. A valid proof cannot thereby forge arbitrary assets, but asking the wallet to submit an unintended valid message is a real user-facing integrity issue, not merely layout quality.

F-14.assessment: Independent discovery executes all 174 tracked JavaScript test files: eight files fail with 11 TAP failures, matching the previous inventory/fixture/discovery issues. Selected required workflows remain green. These stale assertions and environment assumptions do not demonstrate principal theft, but green selected CI must not be described as a complete passing suite.
F-14.evidence: E-02; full results.tsv, individual logs and inherited triage reconciled.

F-15.assessment: Fresh evidence improves release assurance: v3.5.1 download SHA matches its official manifest and public services respond. The sampled RPCs advertise different versions; both report Go 1.23.11 while the published binary manifest records Go 1.23.12. Routed banners are not host checksum attestations, so actual validator/service binary and migration identity remain qualified. Missing host evidence alone is not a protocol NO-GO.
F-15.evidence: E-06; timestamped version/release/health observations and operator rollout assertion.

F-16.assessment: Canonical rereads and the configured second finalized witness remain required before expiry release on external chains. Mismatch and unavailable witness cases retain liabilities. New sponsorship scheduling does not weaken that original repaired gate.
F-16.evidence: E-01, E-02; expiry witness and no-release regressions.

F-17.assessment: Payer/IP/global limits and quote-time budget reservations remain useful bounded controls, but many unpaid payer identities can still occupy finite admission capacity. The new operator admission switch is not an identity or Sybil-resistance mechanism. Existing Medium remains partially mitigated.
F-17.evidence: E-01, E-02; tax-evidence admission/funding queries and sponsorAdmissionState tests.

F-18.assessment: The conservative budget calculation can still count economically overlapping spend and unsettled liabilities in the same window. This may reject legitimate admission; it does not establish under-collateralized token minting or an unauthorized payout.
F-18.evidence: E-01, E-02; unchanged sponsor-funding and quote reservation arithmetic.

F-19.assessment: New admission can now stop while historical grant servicing continues, and manual escalation events are retained. Neither the event ledger nor a reviewer status fulfills, compensates or waives an outstanding promise. Controlled queued-preflight execution also shows the fresh send path can act after external parent completion while waiting for the effect queue, without a final delivery reread. This refines the existing lifecycle cause rather than creating another Medium. No unattended controlled-outcome policy has been accepted on the operator's behalf.
F-19.evidence: E-02, E-08, E-09; source lifecycle plus actual PostgreSQL and controlled transaction-boundary probes.
F-19.remediation: Complete an explicitly approved outcome/escalation workflow with actual fulfillment evidence and accountability. Revalidate relevant current delivery/authorization state at the effect boundary without losing the original prepared transaction or creating blind replacements. Preserve liabilities during uncertainty; treat the review record as evidence, never payment. Correct F-40 metadata attribution separately.

F-20.assessment: The retirement caller now requires an exact same-message current-set successor from the local signer in memory and on disk, rather than inferring success from a nil error. Complete payload comparison includes fee, source/destination identity, registry, gateway and ISM. Persistence synchronizes file and directory before success. New audit tests demonstrate preservation after a blocked successor write and successful restart recovery; wrong/missing/corrupt successors remain rejected. The original consume-before-success cause is closed on the frozen source.
F-20.evidence: E-01, E-03, E-04. Five existing repeated cases and ten supplemental repeated test passes; no physical power-cut test or every-host attestation.
F-20.remediation: Retain exact-payload and durable-journal tests. Complete ordinary host rollout verification and preserve journal data. No new fork, staking migration, contract redeployment or weakening of signing eligibility is required for this recovery patch.

F-21.assessment: A successful but incomplete log response can still advance a durable discovery cursor. Full independent authentication of discovered messages prevents signing invented source activity, but it does not prove that every valid message was discovered. Known-hash recovery mitigates availability, not completeness.
F-21.evidence: E-01, E-03; unchanged event scan/cursor and direct-evidence call graph.

F-22.assessment: Admin reconciliation still uses confirmation-depth acceptance on relevant paths rather than consistently applying the chain-native safe/finalized rule. Explicit finalized handling in supported cases is positive but does not close every L2 path. This is distinct from a mismatch in the live sampled immutable bytecodes.
F-22.evidence: E-01, E-02, E-06; unchanged admin receipt policy.

F-23.assessment: Exclusive deployment locks are removed in ordinary finally handling, but an orphan after process termination can require manual owner/journal diagnosis. The current delta changes neither the lock ownership protocol nor safe recovery, so existing Low remains.
F-23.evidence: E-01, E-02; unchanged exclusive-intent file lifecycle.

F-24.assessment: The paid-fee backfill still constructs an event without the message/transaction identity required by the shared store path. This is an indexing/availability inconsistency, not an independent authorization to move collateral. The relevant source remains unchanged.
F-24.evidence: E-01, E-02; transfer-index-worker caller and store input contract.

F-25.assessment: Dense event windows still lack a complete adaptive progress strategy under provider range/response limits. Failing closed preserves evidence but may stall progress. No delta change or new saturation proof closes this original cause.

F-26.assessment: The exact-pair filtering before the bounded delivery-refresh selection remains in place. The original unrelated-route starvation cause stays resolved; this is separate from incomplete discovery and dense-window findings.
F-26.evidence: E-01, E-02; existing unrelated-row regression and unchanged repaired source.

F-27.assessment: The published v3.5.1 release has explicit version, full commit, toolchain and checksum manifests; the streamed binary digest matches. The original empty CLI version-field source cause remains resolved. Mapping a particular live process to that binary is separately qualified under F-15.
F-27.evidence: E-01, E-03, E-06; release workflow and actual download integrity.

F-28.assessment: The unchanged Solidity build uses 0.8.24 with reviewed compiler settings. Official 0.8.38-era advisories include optimizer conditions potentially relevant to older versions, but no exact affected XITA instruction sequence or deployed miscompilation was demonstrated here. A new compiler release or lint warning is not itself an exploit and does not automatically justify redeployment. Applicability/equivalence remains an Informational assurance task.
F-28.evidence: E-05; official Solidity known-bug/advisory references; no completed corrected-compiler equivalence experiment.

F-29.assessment: Legacy governance/membership submission and receipt paths still contain RPC waits not uniformly governed by the worker cancellation/deadline. Worker shutdown waits for work completion; the F-20 local journal change does not supply cancellation throughout that call graph.
F-29.evidence: E-01, E-03; worker Close and legacy relayer/submit review; no production shutdown fault injection.

F-30.assessment: Alert aging still uses immutable creation age rather than a refreshed reconciliation heartbeat. Real-schema monitoring tests pass, retaining the original cause's closure. This is not evidence that each host actually delivers operator alerts.

F-31.assessment: An authenticated failed destination receipt can still leave a submitted/pending presentation rather than an explicit failed-state recovery action. This remains a user-facing state issue; the source transaction and on-chain replay protection are separate controls.

F-32.assessment: Bounded expiry cleanup for unverified unknown-route request hints remains present. Authenticated votes and attestations are outside that cleanup rule. Original permanent request-file accumulation remains resolved on the existing evidence and unchanged source.
F-32.evidence: E-01, E-03; storage maintenance review and prior negative cases.

F-33.assessment: The original late callback in prepared-transaction recovery remains fixed: timeout races only read work and a late resolution does not initiate replay. Fresh tests retain that negative control. The separate fresh-send waiting/stale-state observations are recorded under existing F-08/F-19, not used to falsely reopen or duplicate this specific original cause.
F-33.evidence: E-02, E-08; zero late effects in timed-out read control.

F-34.assessment: Provisional spendable inclusion and exact recovered grant identity still have the previously recorded divergence/reorg gaps. A one-confirmation usability indication is not final safe settlement. These paths are unchanged and remain distinct from preservation of raw signed bytes.

F-35.assessment: Some out-of-scope observation cases are classified and skipped, but accepted delivery samples with missing profile/context can still prevent complete bounded progress. The new sponsor scheduler does not alter this separate observer. Existing Low remains partially mitigated.
F-35.evidence: E-01, E-02; both optional observer paths and inherited failure cases.

F-36.assessment: UTF-8 byte parity and deterministic unsigned-queue quarantine now work. Nevertheless the earlier deployed/publication branch still processes one item before new queued work, without per-item failure isolation. Two requests accepted by real registration and email confirmation reach deployed state, then fail public-profile validation for three consecutive sweeps and block a valid sibling. The positive control advances that sibling. This is the same original per-item isolation cause, not a new finding; already-deployed token ownership/mint security was not shown compromised.
F-36.evidence: E-02, E-07; actual admission/confirmation/queue/manifest code with mocked external effects.
F-36.remediation: Share complete normalized metadata validation across admission and eventual public-profile generation. Add bounded per-item backoff/quarantine to the already-deployed publication path while retaining every signed transaction and verified token identity. Require valid-sibling progress after repeated publication failures and restart; never redeploy to recover a failed profile publication.

F-37.assessment: The unchanged contact-retention cleanup still removes an unresolved signed Creator deployment record after its retention deadline. A fresh controlled expiry test confirms removal. Personal-contact retention and minimal durable transaction recovery need distinct lifetimes; this finding does not imply a new on-chain mint permission.
F-37.evidence: E-01, E-07; isolated filesystem expiry reproduction.

F-38.assessment: The current two-provider Creator child proof compares a projection that omits the creation block hash. Controlled internally consistent responses at one height with different block hashes are accepted. Owner/supply/feature checks remain intact; the missing canonical block identity prevents treating the comparison as independent canonical provenance.
F-38.evidence: E-01, E-10; actual verifier, controlled RPC views, zero real network writes.

F-39.assessment: The mintable Creator summary retains the no-additional-minting wording in an unchanged presentation branch. Contract configuration and project-only mint authority are separate and pass existing tests. This remains Informational, not a bridge custody vulnerability.
F-39.evidence: E-01, E-02, E-05; unchanged UI wording and Creator contract feature tests.

new_finding.title: Reviewer INSERT privilege permits unbound actor, time and sponsor metadata
new_finding.cause: The reviewer receives table-level INSERT; reviewer/current_user and recorded_at/NOW are defaults rather than enforced provenance, and the obligation foreign key binds only grant_key, not the supplied sponsor identity.
new_finding.assessment: The actual restricted database role can insert an escalation attributed to another operator, a historical timestamp and a different sponsor while referencing a real grant key. The public/manual CLI validates its parameters, but direct use of the same granted database authority bypasses those application-only bindings. UPDATE and private-column reads remain denied. This is a new privileged traceability defect; no payout, signed transaction mutation or bridge asset theft was demonstrated.
new_finding.evidence: E-09: reviewer-role.json and isolated PostgreSQL probe on migration 017.
new_finding.limits: Requires the designated reviewer database authority; not a demonstrated unauthenticated public attack. Financial obligations remain present and the role cannot settle or pay them.
new_finding.remediation: Restrict INSERT columns and enforce actor/time at the database boundary, with immutable sponsor binding to the referenced obligation. A narrow audited procedure or trigger can assign trusted session identity/time. Test direct SQL by the actual least-privileged role; do not broaden grant/payment privileges.
